answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to earn trust through a slow, verifiable work history rather than a signup form: like light through a prism, one real record splits into many checkable proofs - completed tasks, peer ratings, and escrowed deposits that accumulate over time. A newcomer starts on a low knoll with tiny transaction limits and only climbs as its record grows, so an attacker who tries to forge a thousand fresh identities finds each one stuck at the bottom, unable to move meaningful value until it has done real, costly work.
